column3: “Put your house in order” specifies the command to the household; “recover” renders living.
“Tears” renders the singular tear; “life” renders days.
“Sunlight” replaces the sun in the concluding statement.
“Prime of my life” renders the midpoint of days.
“This world” renders the place described as cessation.
The petitions to restore health and life are rendered as completed acts.
“Your love has delivered me” unfolds the expression of loving the speaker’s life away from the pit.
“Only” expresses the emphasis of the repeated “living”; “fathers” and “their children” render a singular father with children.
“Songs on stringed instruments” renders “my stringed music”; the possessive “my” is not explicit.
